title: Augmentation axis computes the characterized sheaf cup product
statement: For an arbitrary family U of opens of a scheme X, a computing resolution pairing D [def-sc-module-cup-resolution-data], comparison data A,B,C [def-sc-cech-cup-resolution-comparison-data], and a bilinear cup satisfying IsModuleCupProduct [def-sc-module-cohomology-cup-product], the product of inverse-iso images of the beta homology classes of Cech cycles a,b equals the inverse-iso image of the beta class of any cycle c whose underlying cochain is cechCupCochain(a,b) [def-sc-cech-cup-product]. Only the augmentation axis is asserted; no existence or alpha formula for a total homology pairing is asserted.

source.place: final diagram; signed total construction of Tag 07MB

proof.text: Apply cupCech_signed_axis_pairing to the six comparison maps and their component equations. This gives a bilinear total homology pairing with both the global-resolution alpha formula and the coefficient-Cech beta formula. Its n2CechCupCochain formula is definitionally equal to cechCupCochain.

The homology projection from cycle kernels is epic, hence surjective by ModuleCat.epi_iff_surjective. Each alpha map is a quasi-isomorphism, so its homology map is an isomorphism and is surjective. Compose these surjections to lift the two beta homology classes to global resolution cycles. D.leibniz shows that the actual section D.pair p q top of these two cycles is a cycle: both differential terms vanish. The alpha_class equations and iso.hom_inv_id identify the inverse-iso images of the beta classes with the sheaf classes of these lifts.

Evaluate the total pairing on the lifted cycles with the alpha formula and on the original coefficient cycles with the beta formula. Substitute the two lift equalities to equate the resulting target homology classes. Apply the inverse target comparison iso and simplify alpha_class and iso.hom_inv_id. Finally use hcup at D and the lifted cycles to rewrite their sheaf cup as the sheaf class of their paired resolution cycle. The resulting equality is the required beta class formula.

theorem cupCechResolution_beta_class_pairing {X : Scheme.{v}} {ι : Type v}
    (U : ι → X.Opens) {F G : X.Modules} (D : CupResolutionPairing F G)
    (A : CupCechResolutionComparison U D.left)
    (B : CupCechResolutionComparison U D.right)
    (C : CupCechResolutionComparison U D.target) (p q : ℕ)
    (cup : (RingedSpace.moduleCohomology X.toRingedSpace p).obj F →ₗ[Γ(X, ⊤)]
      (RingedSpace.moduleCohomology X.toRingedSpace q).obj G →ₗ[Γ(X, ⊤)]
        (RingedSpace.moduleCohomology X.toRingedSpace (p + q)).obj
          (@id X.Modules (F ⊗ G)))
    (hcup : IsModuleCupProduct F G p q cup)
    (a : (((cechComplexFunctor U).obj F.presheafModuleCat).sc
      p).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K)
    (b : (((cechComplexFunctor U).obj G.presheafModuleCat).sc
      q).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K)
    (c : (((cechComplexFunctor U).obj (F ⊗ G).presheafModuleCat).sc
      (p + q)).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K)
    (hc : c.val = cechCupCochain U F G p q a.val b.val) :
    cup ((A.iso p).inv (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap A.beta p (cupCycleClass _ p a)))
      ((B.iso q).inv (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap B.beta q (cupCycleClass _ q b))) =
        (C.iso (p + q)).inv
          (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap C.beta (p + q) (cupCycleClass _ (p + q) c))
